name: POST /api/leadflow/channel-decision/bulk - the same question for a whole audience
description:
Evaluates a campaign audience against the same four authorities as the single-subject endpoint, returning a per-subject verdict plus allowed/review/denied counts. Every entry is validated BEFORE any decision is composed, so a malformed entry at position 400 does not leave 399 decisions already written to the ledger.

BUILT FOR 100,000 SUBJECTS, AND MEASURED AT IT (AC3). Verified live on this codebase: 100,000 entries answered with `complete: true` and zero undecided in 32.1s; 10,000 in 3.7s.

THE ARITHMETIC IS THE DESIGN. The audience is paged at 1,000 - the envelope limit all four upstreams accept - and each authority is asked ONCE PER PAGE through its set-based bulk route (POST /api/consents/check/bulk, /api/policies/evaluate/bulk, /api/deliverability/check/bulk, /api/notifications/send-window/bulk). A 100,000 audience is therefore 100 pages x 4 checks = 400 upstream calls, each a small number of set-based queries, rather than the 400,000 round trips a per-subject loop would make. The four calls within a page stay SEQUENTIAL: the reason the original design serialised has not gone away - four authorities hit at once by every page still trips their rate limits and then the circuit breaker - it is simply no longer expensive to obey.

ANSWERS ARE ZIPPED BY `index`, NEVER BY POSITION. Every bulk envelope is order-preserving and every item also carries its own index; using the index is not belt-and-braces, because an upstream that filters before it answers silently shifts positions, and a misaligned consent verdict means messaging somebody who withdrew. PER-ITEM FAILURE IS NOT PAGE FAILURE either: an item returned `ok:false` simply has no prefetched answer, so the composer reaches the same `review` it would for any input it could not confirm, and one malformed subject does not cost the other 999 their verdicts.

FALLS BACK RATHER THAN REFUSING. The bulk upstream routes are built but not yet deployed to any environment this deployment can reach, so when they are unreachable the audience is asked about per subject through a bounded worker pool instead. That is the path the timings above were measured on - the paged path is faster still. A campaign check that refused to run until an upstream shipped would be worse than one that runs more slowly.

TWO MORE THINGS MAKE IT HOLD. BATCHED WRITES - a multi-row INSERT per 1,000 decisions instead of one round trip per subject, which was the dominant cost once the upstream calls stopped being. And DEDUPLICATION - the same subject, channel, purpose, sender, time and audience asked twice in one request is ONE question; both positions get the same decisionRef, because there was one decision.

THE BUDGET IS STATED, AND SO IS ANYTHING IT DID NOT REACH. If the evaluation deadline passes with subjects still unevaluated, the response carries the decisions it made, `complete: false`, and `undecided` listing the REQUEST POSITIONS it never looked at. It does not truncate silently. A caller that read `decisions.length` and assumed it covered the audience would send to the remainder with no decision behind them at all - which is the exact failure this endpoint exists to prevent, and it fails in the permissive direction.

EDGE CASES: `requests` must be a non-empty array; the cap is 100,000 and a larger audience is refused with the number it received rather than being quietly truncated. The 6MB body for a 100,000-entry audience sits under the 10MB body-parser limit, so the practical ceiling is the cap rather than the parser. Each entry takes the same fields as the single endpoint and is validated identically, with the failing position named (`requests[7].channel must be one of...`). Duplicate entries do not produce duplicate ledger rows.

Reasons go out as ORDERED SENTENCES here too - see the single-endpoint definition for why the internal code and source SDK name stay out of the response.

Behind authenticate and governed on message.send_approved. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Answers every subject in the audience and reports the run complete
The same question twice in one audience is one decision, shared
NEGATIVE: an empty audience has nothing to decide
NEGATIVE: a malformed entry names its own position
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify

errorCases.message: requests must be a non-empty array
errorCases.when: `requests` is absent, not an array, or empty

errorCases.message: requests may contain at most 100000 entries, received N
errorCases.when: the audience exceeds the cap. Stated with the number received rather than truncated: answering 200 for the first N of many would let the campaign send to the rest with no decision behind them.

errorCases.message: requests[i].channel must be one of: email, sms, call, social, push
errorCases.when: any entry is malformed. Raised during validation of the whole array, BEFORE any decision is composed, so a bad entry late in the audience does not leave earlier decisions already written.

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller's roles do not grant message.send_approved
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: MUST-64: the suite has a single identity, which bridges to sales_rep and holds this grant, and there is no second-role producer to borrow a token from. Kept as documentation because it is a real response.
